newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends lower as Tokyo falls.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends lower as Tokyo falls.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended lower as a lower close in Tokyo and sluggish demand dampened sentiment, traders said.

"Falls in Tokyo and the slow buying interest from consumers pulled down prices today," a dealer said, adding that prices may lose further ground if demand remains absent. Dealers noted some enquiries from Asian consumers for SMR grades but no trades were done.
They said SMR CV was offered at 360 cents, SMR L at 340 cents, SMR 5 at 308 cents and drum latex at 239 cents.
Dealers expect a tight supply in the near-term due to the long Chinese Lunar New Year and Moslem Eid al-Fitr holidays which had reduced tapping activities, adding that this may check the price drop.
At the close, both March RSS 1 and March SMR 20 eased two cents to 302 cents ($1.21) and 298 cents a kg respectively.
The INRO five-day moving average was Malaysian/Singapore 234.36 cents a kg on February 14 against 233.26 on February 13. The daily indicator price was 234.29 against 235.61.
